title: Streamlined advisory intake heuristics and enterprise hotline for optimization requests
creator: Amelia Torres
description: Create a single, predictable intake and prioritization path for non-bug optimization requests (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies) with an enterprise hotline for time-sensitive customers. The goal is to reduce TTR for high-value requests, surface safe low-effort levers for customers, and standardize handoffs to Eng/Optimize/Support.
background: Customers regularly request help tuning batching, cache policies, quantization profiles, and routing to meet cost/latency trade-offs. Today intake is ad-hoc across support tickets, CSMs, and sales — causing duplicate work, uneven SLAs, and missed escalation signals from enterprise accounts. Several PMs and Solutions Engineers have highlighted a need for predictable triage that balances engineering capacity with customer SLAs.
scope: Design and ship a triage rubric, an enterprise hotline flow, and a lightweight automation layer that maps request signals to lanes (Self-serve, Concierge, Escalation). Deliverables: intake form template, triage rubric, routing rules for Concierge queue, playbook for hotline escalation, and dashboards to track SLA adherence.
out_of_scope: Building an end-to-end automation engine for knob application, rewiring billing systems, or implementing per-customer private deployments. Deep engineering changes to runtime kernels are out of scope; this ticket focuses on intake and routing only.
acceptance_criteria: A documented triage rubric that classifies requests into Self-serve / Concierge / Escalation lanes with examples
An intake form (Zendesk/Confluence/Typeform prototype) that captures required signals (workload footprint, latency SLO, current model, token distribution, cost sensitivity, security constraints)
Hotline runbook for enterprise customers with SLA targets (initial response <4h, resolution plan within 48h) and contact handoff steps
Automated tag mapping in Support that routes Concierge-lane requests to the Optimization Slack channel and creates a Linear ENG task template
Dashboard in Console showing queue depth, SLA attainment, and top requested Knobs by week
proposal: Adopt a three-lane intake model with a priority-scoring heuristic. Use a lightweight scoring function that combines customer tier (enterprise, paid), estimated impact (tokens/sec, monthly spend), and complexity (requires code change, runtime kernel, or config-only). Enterprise customers meeting a threshold get hotline access which creates a pre-populated Concierge task and notifies the on-call Optimization engineer. Lower-impact requests are routed to Self-serve with docs and suggested knob presets.
tasks: Draft intake form fields and examples (PM)
Define scoring heuristic and thresholds (PM + Optimize Eng)
Create hotline runbook with contact matrix and escalation windows (Customer Success)
Implement Support tag mapping and Linear automation (Engineer - Support Tools)
Add a dashboard panel to Console for advisory queue metrics (Observability)
Pilot with three enterprise customers and iterate (Solutions Eng + CSM)
stakeholders: Jin Wu - Head of Optimize Eng
timeline: MVP design and automation by 2026-03-31. Pilot 4 weeks post-launch. Iterate month-over-month based on SLA attainment and feedback.
impact: Reduces time-to-resolution for enterprise optimization requests, directs engineering effort to highest ROI items, and increases CSAT for performance advisory work. Expected to cut average TTR for Concierge lane from 10 days to 2 days for pilot customers.
open_questions: What exact score threshold should auto-qualify an enterprise request for hotline?
Should the hotline create a reserved engineering block or rely on on-call rotations?
Which support fields are necessary to estimate cost sensitivity without exposing billing data?
How do we prevent gaming of the intake form by customers?
decisions: Three-lane model accepted: Self-serve, Concierge, Escalation
Hotline SLA target set to initial response <4h and a published plan within 48h for Concierge requests
Start with tag-based automation in Support rather than building a new intake service
